city.authors: Geoff Pike and Jyrki Alakuijala · Google
city.background: CityHash is Google’s family of noncryptographic string hashes, drawing on earlier work by Austin Appleby and Bob Jenkins. CityHash64 was designed with short strings and hash-table keys in mind.

farm.background: FarmHash continues Google’s work on fast string hashing after CityHash. The library includes several implementations selected for different processors; the point here is specifically the NA variant’s seeded 64-bit function.

murmur.background: MurmurHash3 belongs to the same project as the original SMHasher test suite. Its name reflects its use of multiplication and rotation. The x64_128 variant maintains two 64-bit state words and returns 128 bits.

mx3.background: mx3 grew out of work on bit mixers and supplies a mixer, a pseudorandom generator, and a string hash. Version 3 revised the hash’s seeding and speed while retaining its multiply-and-xorshift design.

fasthash-64.background: fasthash is a compact C design built around multiplication and xorshift mixing. The project describes its mixing function as learned using genetic programming. It offers both 64-bit and 32-bit outputs.

muse.background: MuseAir is a portable design using widening multiplication. The record here is the historical v0.3 implementation retained in SMHasher3; later upstream algorithm versions must be considered separately.

komi.background: komihash is a header-only C/C++ hash from the author of a5hash. Its multiplication-based design keeps the high and low halves of products in separate state variables and processes long inputs through parallel lanes.

t1ha.background: t1ha (“Fast Positive Hash”) is a family of noncryptographic hashes with separate variants for different platforms and uses. This point is t1ha2’s one-shot 64-bit function, not its streaming or 128-bit API.

a5.background: a5hash is a header-only C/C++ family aimed at hash tables and hash maps, from the author of komihash. It supplies 64-bit and 128-bit functions. Both plotted results concern v5.21.

rapid3.authors: Nicolas De Carli · based on wyhash by Wang Yi
rapid3.background: rapidhash builds on wyhash’s widening-multiplication approach. Its standard, Micro, and Nano variants trade throughput against code size. The plotted benchmark is the standard v3 implementation.

mum.background: MUM stands for “multiply and mix”: it combines the halves of a wide product to mix bits. The project also contains pseudorandom generators. This post studies the pre-fix v3 design with fixed public constants.

mir.background: mir’s hash lives in the MIR compiler project and uses multiplication followed by addition of the high and low halves. It includes native-wide and decomposed-multiplication implementations; this chart uses mir.exact timings.

xxh3-64.authors: Yann Collet and the xxHash contributors
xxh3-64.background: XXH3 extends the xxHash family with 64-bit and 128-bit outputs and optimized paths for different input lengths and CPUs. These results use v0.8.3’s seeded API with the default public secret.

highway.authors: Jyrki Alakuijala, Bill Cox, and Jan Wassenberg · Google
highway.background: Introduced in a 2016 paper, HighwayHash uses SIMD multiplication and permutation with a 256-bit key. It was designed as a fast keyed hash and pseudorandom function, with 64-bit, 128-bit, and 256-bit outputs.

spooky.background: SpookyHash is Jenkins’s noncryptographic 128-bit hash, designed for 64-bit machines, with wrappers for shorter outputs. The V2 revision corrected issues in the original design; this point is its 64-bit wrapper.

pengyhash.background: pengyhash is a compact noncryptographic 64-bit hash built from additions, rotations, and XORs. Version 0.3 uses a 64-bit seed, whereas earlier versions used 32 bits.

nmhash32.background: NMHASH32 and NMHASH32X are separate functions in the hash-garage project. Both return 32 bits and accept a 32-bit seed, but use different mixing designs. The two points retain their own witnesses and measurements.

gx.background: gxhash is a Rust hash designed around hardware AES instructions. It uses parallel processing to obtain high throughput and provides several output widths. This point is the studied 64-bit v3.5.0 implementation.

ahash.background: aHash is a Rust hash-table hasher that uses AES instructions when available, with a separate fallback design. This post’s result is specifically for the AES path in version 0.8.12.

polymur.background: PolymurHash combines polynomial hashing over a prime field with a Murmur-inspired final mixer. It aims to provide a universal hash using ordinary widening multiplication, without requiring carry-less multiplication instructions.

halftimehash-64.background: HalftimeHash’s 2021 paper targets long strings without widening 64-bit multiplication or finite-field arithmetic. The four plotted styles are implementation variants: all return 64-bit hashes, despite the numbers in their names.

umash.background: UMASH was introduced at Backtrace in 2020 to combine fast string hashing with collision bounds. It also computes a second hash alongside the first to produce a 128-bit fingerprint.

clhash.background: CLHASH uses carry-less multiplication instructions to accelerate universal hashing. Its construction was published as “Faster 64-bit universal hashing using carry-less multiplications.”

chain256.authors: Thomas Dybdahl Ahle · author of this post
chain256.background: ChainHash is the author’s construction in the fast-polynomials project. This point uses 256-byte blocks and the model A key distribution, which takes 80 independent random key bytes.

poly1305.background: Poly1305 is the polynomial-hashing component of Bernstein’s Poly1305-AES authenticator. It works modulo 2¹³⁰ − 5 with a restricted (“clamped”) polynomial key and produces a 128-bit tag.

ghash.authors: David A. McGrew and John Viega · GCM construction
ghash.background: GHASH is the universal-hashing component of Galois/Counter Mode (GCM). It evaluates a polynomial over the binary field GF(2¹²⁸); GCM combines that hash with counter-mode encryption.

rows.name: CityHash64 v1.1.1
rows.label: CityHash64
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score.
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit WithSeed seed; structural result also holds for all pairs of 64-bit seeds.
rows.summary: Two different eight-byte messages reach the same public hash before the seed is applied. The seeded wrapper therefore returns the same result for every seed.

rows.name: FarmHash64 NA v1.1
rows.label: FarmHash64 NA
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score.
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit Hash64WithSeed seed; all-seed result also holds for Hash64WithSeeds.
rows.summary: Like CityHash’s seeded wrapper, this variant compresses the message before applying the secret. The eight-byte witness pair already agrees at that point, so changing the seed cannot separate it.

rows.name: MurmurHash3 x64_128
rows.label: MurmurHash3 x64_128
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score.
rows.key_model: Uniform 32-bit API seed; all 2^32 seeds enumerated by the supplied panel.
rows.summary: A controlled difference survives the public word mixing and is cancelled by later message words. The selected pair collides in the full 128-bit output for every 32-bit API seed.

rows.name: mx3 v3
rows.label: mx3 v3
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. This is mx3 v3.0.0, tag 48924ee7, with a 64-bit seed. rurban’s mx3 entry tests v1.0.0 (0x4DB51E5B) with a 32-bit seed cast to 64 bits; its GOOD label and older bad-seed result do not describe the attacked v3.
rows.key_model: 64 (`inline uint64_t hash(const uint8_t* buf, size_t len, uint64_t seed)`; v3 seeds via h = mix_stream(seed, len + 1), v1/v2 via h = seed ^ len). The seed enters only through the additive term C^(L+1)*seed of the pre-finalizer state, before a public bijective finalizer mix(). SMHasher3: 64.
rows.summary: A one-byte message and an eight-byte message cancel their public length and word terms. Both leave the same seed-dependent state, giving an every-seed collision.

rows.name: fasthash-64
rows.label: fasthash-64
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. The unversioned fast-hash code is pinned to upstream commit 08a25db2 (2018-10-22). SMHasher3 verification is 0xA16231A7 at 64 bits and 0xE9481AFC at 32 bits. Its wrappers pass a 64-bit seed to both widths; upstream fasthash32 takes a 32-bit seed. The every-seed identity covers both models, which the reproduction program measures separately.
rows.key_model: 64 for fasthash64 (`uint64_t fasthash64(const void *buf, size_t len, uint64_t seed);` fasthash.h line 50); upstream fasthash32 takes `uint32_t seed` (fasthash.h line 42), so nonzero fixed-pair probabilities are at least 2^-32 under a uniform native seed; SMHasher3 passes a 64-bit seed_t to both widths. The seed enters once, `uint64_t h = seed ^ (len * m);` (fasthash.c line 41 -- corrected from 40), before any message word; each 8-byte word (and the zero-padded tail) passes through the public bijection mix() (xorshift 23, *0x2127599bf4325c37, xorshift 47) and then h = (h ^ mix(v)) * m with odd m = 0x880355f21e6d1965; output mix(h).
rows.summary: The selected seven-byte and eight-byte messages cancel the different length terms before the common finalizer. The same construction collides for every seed at both output widths.

rows.name: fasthash-32
rows.label: fasthash-32
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. The unversioned fast-hash code is pinned to upstream commit 08a25db2 (2018-10-22). SMHasher3 verification is 0xA16231A7 at 64 bits and 0xE9481AFC at 32 bits. Its wrappers pass a 64-bit seed to both widths; upstream fasthash32 takes a 32-bit seed. The every-seed identity covers both models, which the reproduction program measures separately.
rows.key_model: 64 for fasthash64 (`uint64_t fasthash64(const void *buf, size_t len, uint64_t seed);` fasthash.h line 50); upstream fasthash32 takes `uint32_t seed` (fasthash.h line 42), so nonzero fixed-pair probabilities are at least 2^-32 under a uniform native seed; SMHasher3 passes a 64-bit seed_t to both widths. The seed enters once, `uint64_t h = seed ^ (len * m);` (fasthash.c line 41 -- corrected from 40), before any message word; each 8-byte word (and the zero-padded tail) passes through the public bijection mix() (xorshift 23, *0x2127599bf4325c37, xorshift 47) and then h = (h ^ mix(v)) * m with odd m = 0x880355f21e6d1965; output mix(h).
rows.summary: The selected seven-byte and eight-byte messages cancel the different length terms before the common finalizer. The same construction collides for every seed at both output widths.

rows.name: MuseAir v0.3
rows.label: MuseAir
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. SMHasher3 version only. Supplied upstream audit records algorithm v2 / crate 0.6.0 and deprecated earlier versions.
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit seed. Pair collides on both full 128-bit variants and both 64-bit variants.
rows.summary: A public zero-product operand makes a changed message word disappear before secret mixing. The fixed pair collides for every seed in the studied v0.3 implementation.

rows.name: komihash v5.27 / v5.34
rows.label: komihash
rows.scope: Measured score cap with sampling uncertainty; better pairs may exist. This high-probability construction applies to lengths 64..127 bytes only; not an all-length probability.
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit UseSeed.
rows.summary: Two messages differing in just two bits collide for about 91.06% of sampled seeds. Public relations between lanes allow the changes to cancel. This construction applies only to lengths 64–127 bytes.

rows.name: t1ha2_atonce-64 v2.1.4
rows.label: t1ha2_atonce-64
rows.scope: Measured score cap with sampling uncertainty; better pairs may exist. Cross-length 16/11-byte pair. Exact class density 2^-26 multiplied by measured conditional rate about 2^-4. Equal-length best claim not independently re-run; excluded.
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit one-shot API seed.
rows.summary: The 16-byte and 11-byte witness messages exploit carry patterns for a structured class of seeds. The cap combines an exact class size with a measured success rate inside that class.

rows.name: a5hash v5.21, 64-bit
rows.label: a5hash 64-bit
rows.evidence: collides for at least 118 of every 2^45 keys (counted)
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. Exact sufficient seed class, not equality for total epsilon. Best verified score upper bound, not an exhaustive minimum over lengths. v5.25 not vector-checked.
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit UseSeed.
rows.summary: An exactly counted class of seeds makes a multiplication erase a message word. This proves a lower bound on one pair’s collision probability, and therefore an upper cap on the family’s score.

rows.name: a5hash v5.21, 128-bit
rows.label: a5hash 128-bit
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. Additional variant, not one of the original ten entries.
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit UseSeed; both full output words collide.
rows.summary: A public zero-product operand erases a changed word for every seed. Both output words collide, despite this tested 128-bit variant passing all 250 published SMHasher3 tests.

rows.name: rapidhash v3
rows.label: rapidhash v3
rows.scope: Measured score cap with sampling uncertainty; better pairs may exist. SMHasher3 tests v3. The first-fold flaw persists in standard, -micro and -nano: each has 11/2^30 at both 32 B and 48 B. The 28.54-bit plotted cap uses L=4 at 32 B; the 48-byte score is 29.125530882083858. Timings shown are for standard v3; protected variants were not measured by this reproduction. Exact Poisson 95% interval for this witness-derived score: [27.7, 29.5].
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit API seed (sampled reproducibly with xoshiro256**); fixed default public secret/constants
rows.summary: Complementing both operands of an early multiplication can leave its high/low fold unchanged. The measured pair gives an upper cap, not a ranking against other hashes whose searches used different budgets.

rows.name: MUM v3
rows.label: MUM v3
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. Exact multiplication, fixed public constants, pre-fix MUM v3. The key-free 8-byte pair collides for both 8-word and 16-word unroll variants. The plotted speed is mum3.exact.unroll3 (8 words), from the two-host benchmark. Its unroll4 timings are not substituted. This does not describe the later collision-prevention default.
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit API seed (sampled reproducibly with xoshiro256**); fixed default public secret/constants
rows.summary: Two distinct eight-byte words have the same public multiplication fold before they meet the seeded state. The every-seed result concerns pre-fix MUM v3, not the later collision-prevention default.

rows.name: mir.exact / mir.inexact
rows.label: mir.exact / mir.inexact
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. mir has no algorithm version number; its arithmetic is unchanged since April 2019. SMHasher3 mir.exact (0x00A393C8) and mir.inexact (0x422A66FC) are output-equivalent to upstream mir_hash and mir_hash_strict on little-endian hosts. The strict fold drops one cross-product carry; it does not drop every carry. The 64-bit seed is passed verbatim, including seed+len = 0; SMHasher3’s inexact seed-fixup is a harness option, not the API model here. The chart uses only mir.exact timings from the two-host benchmark.
rows.key_model: 64 (`uint64_t seed`, entering only as `uint64_t r = seed + len;`, mir-hash.h line 67); every message word enters only through the public fold mum(v, p_i) XORed into the state (p1 = 0x65862b62bdf5ef4d, p2 = 0x288eea216831e6a7). SMHasher3: 64 (mir.inexact carries seedfixfn excludeBadseeds for len+seed == 0, a harness fixup only).
rows.summary: Two eight-byte words yield the same zero public fold, leaving identical seeded states. The selected pair works in both the exact and inexact implementations.

rows.name: XXH3-64 0.8.3
rows.label: XXH3-64 0.8.3
rows.scope: Measured score cap with sampling uncertainty; better pairs may exist. The rate depends on the first two words. Changing bytes 16 onward changes the output, not the colliding-seed set. No practical flooding attack is established by this approximately 2^-21 fixed-pair rate. Approximate 95% sampling half-width: ±0.09 bits. This measurement establishes no rate or guarantee for independently randomized custom-secret APIs.
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit API seed (sampled reproducibly with xoshiro256**); fixed default public secret/constants
rows.summary: Complementing the first two words can preserve their multiplication fold. The measured cap comes from a selected fixed pair; it is not a demonstrated flooding attack or a result for independently randomized custom secrets.

rows.name: XXH3-128 0.8.3
rows.label: XXH3-128 0.8.3
rows.scope: Measured score cap with sampling uncertainty; better pairs may exist. Pair F sets w1=~w0 before complementing both words, preserving their sum. Both low64 and high64 are compared; this is a full 128-bit collision. Exact Poisson 95% interval for this witness-derived score: [28.5, 31.3]. This measurement establishes no rate or guarantee for independently randomized custom-secret APIs.
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit API seed (sampled reproducibly with xoshiro256**); fixed default public secret/constants
rows.summary: The selected pair preserves both an early product fold and the relevant word sum. Both halves of the 128-bit output are compared: the measured collisions are full-output collisions.

rows.name: HighwayHash-64, frozen
rows.label: HighwayHash-64
rows.evidence: collides for at least 56,165 of every 2^72 keys (counted class contribution)
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. Conservative 96-byte headline witness. Exact sufficient-event contribution, not exact total collision probability. All 64/128/256 output widths inherit it. Original second-family capped sample confirmed pair but not exact numerator.
rows.key_model: Full uniform 256-bit HHKey, four independent 64-bit words.
rows.summary: A rare, explicitly counted key event lets a 96-byte pair merge the entire internal state before finalization. The cap uses that sufficient event; it is not an exact total collision probability.

rows.name: SpookyHash V2-64
rows.label: SpookyHash V2-64
rows.scope: Measured score cap with sampling uncertainty; better pairs may exist. The same pair collides on SpookyHash2-32 at the same measured rate, and on both 64-bit halves. SMHasher3 duplicates a 64-bit seed; native Hash32 takes a 32-bit seed. Exact half balance is unproved. The claimed 2^32 and independent-seed-word runs were not independently reproduced.
rows.key_model: Hash64 duplicates one uniform seed into both native seed words. Similar rate measured with independent 128-bit native seeds.
rows.summary: A late-injected difference cancels in the internal state before finalization. The selected pair collides for about half the sampled seeds; exact half balance has not been proved.

rows.name: pengyhash v0.3
rows.label: pengyhash v0.3
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. The attacked function is SMHasher3’s sequenced pengyhash v0.3, verification 0x861A1254, with a 64-bit seed. The task’s original v0.2 label and rurban’s v0.2 results concern an older 32-bit-seed implementation. Upstream v0.3 has a reported unsequenced modification; this result is pinned to the sequenced SMHasher3 form. v0.3 uses GPLv3; earlier versions used BSD 2-Clause.
rows.key_model: 64 (`uint64_t pengyhash(const void *p, size_t size, uint64_t seed);` pengyhash.h line 7; 32 in v0.1/v0.2). The seed enters only in the 6-round finalization (`s[1] += f[1] + seed` each round, with the 0..31-byte zero-padded tail f -- corrected from '<=32'); the 32-byte bulk loop is seed-free, so the 256-bit state after it is a public function of the message and its length (s0 = size). SMHasher3: 64.
rows.summary: The bulk loop never uses the seed. Two messages reach the same public state before seeded finalization, so they collide for every seed. This record uses SMHasher3’s sequenced v0.3 implementation.

rows.name: nmhash32 v2
rows.label: nmhash32 v2
rows.evidence: collides for 1,078,944,392 of every 2^32 keys (exhaustively counted)
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. NMHASH32 v2 uses a 32-bit seed and returns 32 bits. Verification is 0x12A30553. The last algorithmic change was 2021-06-08; the 2021-06-09 commit changed the version label, and the December 2024 undefined-behaviour fix preserved verification values. The new timings use scalar code on M2 Pro and AVX-512 on Xeon; the reproduction is scalar.
rows.key_model: 32 (`uint32_t seed`, nmhash.h line 593; author on issue #2: 'output size is fixed to 32bit. seed is also 32bit.'; SMHasher3 FLAG_HASH_SMALL_SEED). The seed enters only as sl = seed+len (9..255 B: four lanes y_j = sl ^ word; 0..8 B: seed+const added to the data and rotl(seed,5) XORed mid-mixer). For a uniform 32-bit seed, fixed-pair probabilities are integer multiples of 2^-32; nonzero probabilities are at least 2^-32, not at most that value.
rows.summary: A difference passes through a lane under specific seed-bit and carry conditions, then cancels in later words. Exhaustive enumeration counts the successful seeds; this is not the every-seed result of NMHASH32X.

rows.name: nmhash32x v2
rows.label: nmhash32x v2
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. NMHASH32X v2 is a separate function from NMHASH32, with 32×32 short-key multiplication, a 32-bit seed, 32-bit output and verification 0xA8580227. It has its own row and witness. Its statistical failures and host-specific timings must not be merged with NMHASH32’s; these timings use scalar code on M2 Pro and AVX-512 on Xeon.
rows.key_model: 32 (same `uint32_t seed` API as NMHASH32; SMHasher3 FLAG_HASH_SMALL_SEED). For 9..255 B the y and b streams are affine in (seed, message) and the seed meets the x stream only through y. For a uniform 32-bit seed, fixed-pair probabilities are integer multiples of 2^-32; nonzero probabilities are at least 2^-32, not at most that value.
rows.summary: A controlled difference becomes a top-bit change through public mixing. Two later message words cancel both state differences for every seed.

rows.name: gxhash-64 v3.5.0
rows.label: gxhash-64
rows.scope: Exact sufficient contribution; other pairs or collision events may lower the score. 15 versus 16 bytes. Equal-length 24-byte witness gives 1.585 bits; both verified.
rows.key_model: Uniform 64-bit seed; public-compression collision also defeats full 128-bit output.
rows.summary: The selected 15-byte and 16-byte inputs collide in public compression before the seed can distinguish them. The resulting pair collides for every seed.

rows.name: aHash 0.8.12, AES path
rows.label: aHash AES
rows.scope: Measured score cap with sampling uncertainty; better pairs may exist. Score uses verifier pool 2616/2^31 in heur_panel synthesis. Original 1227/2^30 and second family 75/2^26 are compatible sampling estimates. Approximate 95% sampling half-width: ±0.06 bits.
rows.key_model: Four independent uniform internal RandomState words in the validated C reproduction of the specified aHash 0.8.12 AES path; native Rust transfer is conditional on the operation and constructor mapping.
rows.summary: A chosen difference cancels in both the AES and shuffled-addition accumulators. The measured result uses four independent internal key words in the validated C reproduction; transfer to native Rust depends on the operation and constructor mapping.

rows.name: PolymurHash 2.0
rows.label: PolymurHash 2.0
rows.scope: Uniform k on the exact restricted set K; fixed tweak; full 64-bit output. The key-cardinality gap was resolved with a rigorous lower bound. Shipped seed distribution and almost-strong-universality claim remain uncertified.
rows.key_model: Uniform k on the exact restricted set K; fixed tweak; full 64-bit output. The key-cardinality gap was resolved with a rigorous lower bound. Shipped seed distribution and almost-strong-universality claim remain uncertified.
rows.summary: The audit recovers a full-output guarantee using a rigorous lower bound on the allowed key set’s size. It requires a uniform key from that restricted set; the shipped seed distribution and stronger ASU claim remain uncertified.
